title: Power System Analysis
author: John J. Grainger & William D. Stevenson Jr.
description: The standard reference for steady-state analysis. The load flow and symmetrical components chapters are where I go first when something isn't making sense.

title: Distribution System Modeling and Analysis
author: William H. Kersting
description: The distribution book. Takes unbalanced multi-phase modelling seriously instead of treating it as a footnote to transmission analysis, which is why it's indispensable once you leave the positive-sequence world.

title: Power System Stability and Control
author: Prabha Kundur
description: Dense, and worth the effort. I'm working through it ahead of Semester 2 rather than alongside it.

title: Electrical Power Systems Quality
author: Dugan, McGranaghan, Santoso & Beaty
description: Practical rather than theoretical, with real measurement case studies. Pairs well with a standards document that tells you the limits but not what the waveform actually looks like.

title: Power Generation, Operation and Control
author: Allen J. Wood, Bruce F. Wollenberg & Gerald B. Sheblé
description: Economic dispatch, unit commitment and OPF, explained with the operational context that makes the optimisation problems feel motivated rather than arbitrary.

title: OpenDSS
author: EPRI
description: Free distribution system simulator. Genuinely good at unbalanced multi-phase modelling, and scriptable from Python for batch studies. The documentation rewards persistence.

title: pandapower
description: Python power system analysis built on pandas. My reference implementation for checking my own solver — if my numbers disagree with pandapower, my numbers are wrong.

title: MATPOWER
description: MATLAB package for load flow and OPF. Also the most convenient source of clean IEEE test case data, even when you're working in Python.

title: IEEE PES Test Feeder Cases
description: The standard test feeders — 13-bus, 34-bus, 123-bus and more — with published results. If a method can't reproduce these, it isn't ready for anything else.

title: IEEE Std 519 — Harmonic Control in Electric Power Systems
description: The harmonic limits standard. Read it directly rather than trusting a summary — the TDD-versus-THD distinction is routinely misquoted in specifications.

title: IEEE Std 1547 — Interconnection of Distributed Energy Resources
description: Governs how distributed generation connects to the grid. The 2018 revision's volt-var and volt-watt requirements matter directly to hosting capacity results.

title: NREL National Solar Radiation Database
description: Free irradiance and meteorological time series. What I use to build clear-sky index features for PV forecasting.

title: Energy Forecasting — Tao Hong's blog and GEFCom archives
description: The competition datasets and the methodology writing around them are a better education in forecasting practice than most textbooks.

title: IEEE Power & Energy Society
description: Student membership pays for itself in conference access alone, and the technical committee reports are a fast way to see what the field currently cares about.
